chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub from Malik ibn Atiyya from Dawud ibn Farqad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that in...

what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him): 'O Musa ibn Imran! I have not created a creature more beloved to Me than My believing servant. Indeed, I test him for what is better for him, and I grant him health for what is better for him, and I turn away from him what is evil for him for what is better for him, and I am more Knowing of what suits My servant. So let him be patient with My afflictions, and let him be grateful for My bounties, and let him be pleased with My judgement. I shall record him among the truthful ones in My Presence when he acts by My pleasure and obeys My command.'
ai.seo_question: What is the wisdom behind Allah testing believers according to the Hadith of Musa?
ai.summary: This Hadith Qudsi, recorded in Al-Kafi, highlights the divine wisdom behind trials (balā’) and blessings (ni‘am), framing them as acts of mercy from a God who knows best what is suitable for His servants. It underscores the Shia emphasis on sabr (patience) and shukr (gratitude) as complementary virtues that lead to the high spiritual station of al-Siddiqin (the truthful). The text serves as a theological foundation for understanding divine decree (qadā’) not as arbitrary fate, but as a purposeful mechanism for spiritual refinement and ultimate good.
